NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, critically dependent on TSMC for leading-edge chip fabrication and HBM memory suppliers for GPU performance, while commanding extraordinary pricing power over hyperscalers, cloud providers, and OEMs who compete aggressively to secure GPU allocations. Its dominant position in AI accelerators (estimated 80%+ market share in AI training GPUs) makes it both a bottleneck and an enabler of the global AI infrastructure buildout, giving it exceptional leverage over both upstream supply partners and downstream customers.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of the consumer electronics supply chain, acting as a powerful orchestrator that designs its own silicon and software but relies on a concentrated network of Asian semiconductor fabs and component suppliers — most critically TSMC — for physical manufacturing. On the downstream side, Apple sells primarily direct-to-consumer and through carrier/retail partners, while its high-margin Services segment creates a secondary revenue stream from platform participants like Google and Meta who pay to access Apple's enormous installed base.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of the semiconductor value chain as a vertically integrated manufacturer of DRAM and NAND memory, depending heavily on a concentrated group of semiconductor equipment suppliers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) for its capital-intensive fab operations. On the demand side, Micron's revenue is increasingly driven by AI and cloud infrastructure customers (particularly NVIDIA for HBM) alongside traditional mobile OEMs, making it a critical enabler of the AI compute buildout while remaining exposed to cyclical memory pricing dynamics.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM occupies a uniquely asset-light position at the apex of the semiconductor value chain, monetizing its CPU/GPU IP through licensing fees and per-chip royalties rather than manufacturing anything itself, making its primary dependencies on EDA software vendors like Synopsys and Cadence rather than physical material suppliers. Its downstream reach is extraordinarily broad — virtually every smartphone, cloud server, and IoT device shipped globally embeds an ARM-architecture core, giving the company leverage over the entire semiconductor ecosystem from hyperscalers designing custom silicon to fabless chip companies shipping billions of units annually.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits in the middle of the data infrastructure semiconductor value chain, acting as a fabless chip designer that relies heavily on TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and ARM/EDA vendors for IP and design tools. It primarily serves hyperscale cloud operators (Amazon, Google, Microsoft) and infrastructure OEMs with custom ASICs, Ethernet networking silicon, and storage controllers, making it a critical enabler of AI data center buildouts and high-speed connectivity.
